name: Chungqua's premises seen from the portico of the East India Company's 'factory' at Guangzhou (Canton)
dimensions: Dimensions taken from <u>Victoria & Albert Museum Department of Prints and Drawings and Department of Paintings, Accessions 1928. </u> London: HMSO, 1929
summary: A drawing taken in Guangzhou (Canton) from the portico of the East India Company's trading base, known as a 'factory' or 'hong', looking eastward.  Across the crowded square can be seen the 'hong' of the Cantonese merchant known as Chungqua; its distinctive Chinese roof was removed in the mid-1830s
